sugestoes.texto: WHAT: The sync branch returns a native fetch Response instead of the response shape expected by SDK- and Axios-based callers. WHY: Google reads res.data.access_token, Zoho reads tokenInfo.data.error, and HubSpot reads accessToken directly, so enabling synchronization causes token refresh failures or undefined token values. HOW: Parse the sync response and normalize it at each adapter boundary to the same shape returned by its refresh delegate.

WHAT: Computed keys made from Zod schema toString() values do not validate or preserve arbitrary token response fields. WHY: The object parser strips real expiry and metadata fields such as expires_in, expiry_date, scope, and token_type; Zoom subsequently computes NaN expiry and Office365 loses refreshed expiry information. HOW: Declare the supported expiry fields explicitly and use passthrough() to retain provider-specific fields.

WHAT: The credential update now stores the safeParse result envelope rather than the parsed token data. WHY: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns { success, data }, so the next GoogleCalendarService construction fails googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key) because access_token and other token fields are nested under data, including when synchronization is disabled. HOW: Store the successful result's data property.

WHAT: Bigin passes the credential record ID as the synchronization helper's userId argument. WHY: The helper sends this value as calcomUserId, requesting another user's tokens when IDs differ and routing team credentials through user synchronization as well. HOW: Thread credential.userId from biginAuth into refreshAccessToken and pass that value to refreshOAuthTokens.

WHAT: The new credential update references prisma without importing or declaring it. WHY: Searching this Salesforce module found only this usage, so type checking fails and executing the update raises ReferenceError. HOW: Import the Prisma client from @calcom/prisma.

WHAT: getClient now unconditionally refreshes Salesforce tokens and writes credentials on every service construction. WHY: The constructor always calls getClient, even for valid access tokens, adding a token-endpoint round trip and database write to each instance; the resulting jsforce connection still receives credentialKey.access_token rather than the refreshed token. HOW: Retain the existing jsforce-managed refresh flow or refresh only when necessary and initialize the connection with the refreshed token.

The webhook authenticates requests using a direct string inequality comparison against CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET. String equality is not guaranteed to execute in constant time, exposing a timing oracle for the shared authentication secret on an endpoint that can overwrite user integration credentials. Validate that the supplied header is a string and compare fixed-length digests of the supplied and configured secrets with crypto.timingSafeEqual (or use an equivalent constant-time secret verification helper).

These comments promise that arbitrary numeric properties are recognized as expiry and that other response properties are allowed. In a z.object shape, however, z.string().toString() produces a literal property name; it does not match arbitrary keys. Zod objects also strip unrecognized properties by default. Consequently an integrator following this documented minimum-response contract can lose the expiry field instead of having it recognized. Align the schema and comments by specifying the supported expiry fields and explicitly preserving additional fields.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the entire safeParse result ({ success: true, data: ... }), not the credential object returned by the previous schema.parse call. Passing that result as key stores a wrapper without top-level access_token, refresh_token or expiry_date, breaking subsequent loads even when sharing is disabled. Persist the successful result's data instead.

The sync branch returns a raw Fetch Response, but changed Google code reads res.data.access_token and Hubspot treats the return value as a HubspotToken; Zoho consumers likewise read .data. Enabling synchronization therefore makes these refreshes fail or consume undefined token fields. Adapt the sync response to each caller's expected representation (or normalize both branches and update all callers); do not return the same raw Response to both fetch-style and SDK-style consumers.

refreshOAuthTokens declares its third argument as userId and serializes it as calcomUserId to the sync endpoint, but this call passes credentialId. Credential IDs are not user IDs, so synchronized refresh targets the wrong user or fails to find one. Pass the owning user's ID, preserving null for team-owned credentials.

The previous googleCredentialSchema.parse call returned the credential object itself, but parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the safeParse result ({ success: true, data: ... }). Passing that wrapper as key stores credentials without top-level access_token/refresh_token fields, breaking subsequent credential loading even when sharing is disabled. Persist the helper result's data instead.

The sync branch returns an unparsed fetch Response, whereas the fallback preserves each provider's existing return contract. Google reads res.data, HubSpot expects a HubspotToken object, and Zoho/Bigin read tokenInfo.data. With syncing enabled these consumers receive a Response instead, so their refresh paths fail or read invalid token fields. Adapt the sync response at those consumers (Google/Zoho need a data envelope and HubSpot needs the parsed body), while preserving Response returns for consumers that already parse fetch responses.

refreshOAuthTokens defines its third argument as userId and serializes it as calcomUserId, but this caller supplies credentialId. These IDs identify different records, so enabling sync requests another user's tokens or fails to locate the intended user. Pass the owning credential's userId (and preserve null for team credentials), rather than the credential record ID.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the safeParse result ({ success: true, data: ... }), not the parsed credential object. Passing that entire result as Prisma's key replaces the stored Google credentials with a wrapper, so subsequent readers no longer find access_token, expiry_date, or refresh_token at the top level. Persist its data property instead.

The enabled sync branch returns a native fetch Response without decoding it. Google immediately reads res.data.access_token, Zoho reads tokenInfo.data.error, and HubSpot expects token properties directly. Those contracts worked with their original SDK/Axios return values, but a fetch Response supplies neither shape: Google and Zoho throw on undefined data and HubSpot receives undefined token fields. Decode the endpoint response and adapt it to each caller's expected shape (or normalize both helper paths and all callers to one token-data contract).

Computed property names using Zod schemas' toString() produce literal property names, not wildcard field validators. Consequently a normal response such as { access_token, expires_in } does not preserve expires_in: z.object strips unrecognized fields. In sync mode this loses the expiry required by Office365 and Zoom (and Google's expiry_date), leaving refreshed credentials without a usable updated expiration. Explicitly model the supported expiry fields and preserve additional provider fields with passthrough instead.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the safeParse result ({ success, data }), whereas the previous schema.parse returned the credential object itself. Writing that wrapper to key removes access_token and refresh_token from the top-level stored credential, breaking subsequent authentication even when credential sharing is disabled. Persist the parsed data instead.

The sync branch returns a native fetch Response, but Google reads res.data, HubSpot reads token fields directly, and the Zoho consumers read response.data. With sharing enabled these consumers receive neither shape and token refresh fails. Decode and adapt the sync payload per integration (while preserving Response for the fetch-based consumers), rather than substituting a raw Response for every provider's return value.

z.string().toString() is a literal object property name, not a wildcard for arbitrary response fields. Both computed keys normally stringify to the same name, so the latter overwrites the numeric validator. Because z.object strips unknown fields, normal expires_in/expiry_date fields are discarded (as is refresh_token) in sharing mode. Define the supported expiry fields explicitly and retain the required token fields instead of using schema instances as property names.

refreshOAuthTokens names its third parameter userId and sends it as calcomUserId to the sync endpoint. This call instead passes credentialId. These independent IDs need not match, causing refresh requests for the wrong user (or no user) when sync is enabled. Pass the owning credential's userId, including null for team credentials.

issues.descricao: The new app-credential webhook checks its shared secret with a plain !== string comparison instead of a constant-time comparison, leaking timing information about the secret.

comentarios.texto: Direct !== comparison of webhook secret leaks via timing attack. Use constant-time comparison (e.g., crypto.timingSafeEqual on hashed/buffered values with length check) instead of `req.headers[...] !== process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`.

The webhook authenticates a secret using direct string inequality, which is not constant-time and can leak information about the secret through comparison timing. Compare fixed-length representations using a constant-time primitive (such as crypto.timingSafeEqual), handling absent or malformed headers safely, instead of comparing the secret strings directly.

The webhook secret is compared with the `!==` operator, which short-circuits on the first differing byte and leaks the secret via response timing (timing attack). An attacker can iteratively recover CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET and then forge requests that create/update arbitrary user credential keys (decrypted with the AES key) via this endpoint. Use a constant-time comparison, e.g. crypto.timingSafeEqual on equal-length buffers, guarding for length mismatch first.

issues.descricao: The webhook parses the body with zod .parse and decrypts/JSON-parses the keys without error handling, so invalid payloads produce 500 errors instead of 400 responses.
issues.textoGolden: The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: zod parse, symmetricDecrypt and JSON.parse throw unhandled (no try/catch) with no method guard. WHY: Invalid body/keys or GET request crashes handler with 500 and leaks stack, instead of 400/405. HOW: Wrap parse/decrypt in try/catch returning 400 and restrict to POST.

schema .parse plus symmetricDecrypt/JSON.parse throw unhandled (ZodError, decrypt error, SyntaxError) on invalid body or tampered keys, crashing webhook with 500. Use safeParse and try/catch with 400 responses.

issues.descricao: The webhook's non-atomic findFirst-then-create lets concurrent deliveries for the same user and app insert duplicate credential rows.

comentarios.texto: The webhook performs a non-atomic findFirst followed by create when no credential exists. Concurrent deliveries for the same user and app can both observe no row and insert duplicates because Credential has no unique userId/appId constraint; subsequent findFirst updates only one duplicate, leaving competing credentials stale. Serialize the lookup/create operation for each user/app pair or introduce an appropriate uniqueness constraint and atomic upsert.

issues.descricao: parseRefreshTokenResponse writes the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when the refresh response omits a refresh token, so the stored credential gets an invalid refresh token and later refreshes fail.
issues.textoGolden: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.

comentarios.texto: The parser fabricates the literal refresh token "refresh_token" whenever a successful response omits refresh_token, including when synchronization is disabled. Office365's response schema explicitly permits that omission, and its caller merges parsed data over existing credentials, replacing the valid saved refresh token with this invalid value and breaking the next refresh. Leave the property absent so the existing token survives the merge.

When a refresh response omits refresh_token, this helper manufactures the hardcoded credential "refresh_token". Callers such as Office365 merge this into stored credentials, overwriting the valid existing refresh token and causing subsequent provider refreshes to use a predictable invalid token. Leave the field absent and preserve the existing credential when omission is allowed by the provider, or reject the response when a refresh token is required; do not substitute a literal authentication token.

WHAT: Missing refresh_token is replaced with literal string "refresh_token". WHY: Stores bogus refresh token in DB, breaking all future refreshes and masking provider errors. HOW: Preserve existing credential refresh_token or throw instead of injecting placeholder.

issues.descricao: minimumTokenResponseSchema uses computed keys from z.string().toString(), which produce a literal key rather than a wildcard, so the sync-mode schema does not validate or keep expiry and other token fields as intended.
issues.textoGolden: The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.

comentarios.texto: `[z.string().toString()]` evaluates to a fixed string key such as "ZodString", so minimumTokenResponseSchema requires a literal numeric property with that name. Every synced token response fails validation and throws "Invalid refreshed tokens were returned". Use `z.object({access_token: z.string()}).passthrough()` instead.

The computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` evaluate to the literal string "[object Object]", not a wildcard. The schema therefore requires a numeric property named "[object Object]", so safeParse always fails in credential-sync mode and the function throws "Invalid refreshed tokens were returned". Use `.passthrough()` on an object with access_token and optional numeric expiry fields instead.

The computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` evaluate to a literal string like "ZodString" and not to a wildcard. The schema therefore requires a numeric property with that nonsense name and never matches real token responses. In sync mode every refresh throws "Invalid refreshed tokens were returned". Use `.passthrough()` and a real expiry check instead.

issues.descricao: In sync mode refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response, but callers expect their provider-specific shapes (res.data, axios .data, HubspotToken), so token refresh breaks for Google, Zoho and HubSpot when credential sharing is on.
issues.textoGolden: When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.

comentarios.texto:
WHAT: In the credential-sharing branch `refreshOAuthTokens` returns the raw `fetch` `Response` object instead of a parsed token payload, yet several callers treat the result as an already-parsed token object.
WHY: Callers such as hubspot (`hubspotRefreshToken.expiresIn`), zoho-bigin (`tokenInfo.data.error`), zohocrm (`zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error`) and googlecalendar (`res?.data`) read `.data`/token fields off the return value; a `Response` has neither, so the sync path yields `undefined`/`NaN` or throws a TypeError — the feature's primary code path is broken for those apps.
HOW: Parse the response (e.g. `const data = await response.json(); return data;`) before returning, or make every caller await the appropriate response handler.

In sharing mode refreshOAuthTokens returns the raw fetch Response (no `.data`), but the google caller reads `res?.data` and then `token.access_token`, throwing a TypeError swallowed by the catch, so the token is never refreshed.

`res?.data` assumes the value returned by refreshOAuthTokens has a `.data` field (true for the `fetchTokens.res` branch), but when APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED the helper returns a raw `fetch()` Response, which has no `.data`. Then `token.access_token` throws. Either parse the shared-mode Response here or have refreshOAuthTokens return a normalized `{ data }` shape.

issues.descricao: Google Calendar persists the safeParse result object instead of its data as the credential key, corrupting the stored credential so later reads fail.
issues.textoGolden: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.

comentarios.texto: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a SafeParse result {success,data}, not the parsed key. Storing it directly as `key` writes the wrapper to the credential. Unwrap like other callers: check .success and use .data.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns SafeParse result {success,data}, but call site stores that wrapper as credential `key` (previously googleCredentialSchema.parse() returned the plain object). Store `key.data` / handle wrapper, otherwise persisted credential becomes {success,data} shape and subsequent credential reads fail.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns SafeParse wrapper {success,data} but code stores the whole wrapper as credential.key. Office365calendar in same PR unwraps via .data. Persisted credential will be {success,data} instead of tokens, so next load fails validation. Unwrap to .data after success check.

issues.descricao: After switching to parseRefreshTokenResponse, the tokenResponse.success check in Office365 refreshAccessToken is dead code and the previous error logging was dropped.

comentarios.texto: parseRefreshTokenResponse now throws when parsing fails, so the `tokenResponse.success` check on the next line is dead code and the previous error logging was removed. A failed refresh now throws out of refreshAccessToken instead of keeping the old credentials. Catch the error or restore the previous handling.

issues.descricao: Salesforce getClient now refreshes the OAuth token and writes the credential on every service construction, adding a network round trip and DB write even when the access token is valid.

comentarios.texto: getClient now unconditionally exchanges the Salesforce refresh token on every service construction, even when the saved access token is valid. Each constructor invocation adds a blocking OAuth network round trip and credential database write before any Salesforce operation, replacing jsforce's existing on-demand refresh behavior. Keep refresh on demand or guard the exchange with a token-expiration check.

issues.descricao: The new Salesforce token refresh uses prisma without importing it, so the code fails type checking and throws a ReferenceError at runtime.

comentarios.texto: The new credential update references prisma without importing or declaring it; searching this file finds only the new usage. This fails TypeScript checking and raises ReferenceError after a successful token exchange at runtime. Import prisma from @calcom/prisma before using it.

issues.descricao: Zoho Bigin passes the credential id instead of the user id to refreshOAuthTokens, so the sync endpoint receives the wrong calcomUserId.
issues.textoGolden: The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.

comentarios.texto:
WHAT: The 3rd argument to `refreshOAuthTokens` is `credentialId` (= `credential.id`, line 53), but the function's parameter is `userId` (`refreshOAuthTokens(refreshFunction, appSlug, userId)`).
WHY: When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED, the sync endpoint is sent `calcomUserId: <credential id>` instead of the user id, so Bigin credentials are synced against the wrong/non-existent user (all other apps correctly pass `credential.userId`).
HOW: Pass `credential.userId` instead of `credentialId` as the third argument.

refreshOAuthTokens' third parameter is the Cal.com userId (used as `calcomUserId` in the sync request and to decide whether sharing runs), but this call passes `credentialId`. Every other caller passes `credential.userId`, so the credential-sync endpoint receives a credential row id as the user id and shared credentials are fetched/updated for the wrong identity. Pass `credential.userId` here.

refreshOAuthTokens' third parameter is `userId` (declared in refreshOAuthTokens.ts line 3 and used as `calcomUserId: userId.toString()`), but this call passes `credentialId` (the Credential row id, line 53) instead of the user id. When credential sharing is enabled the customer's sync endpoint receives a credential id labelled as calcomUserId and cannot resolve the correct Cal.com user. Pass `credential.userId` (the BiginToken/credential payload carries it) or plumb the user id through refreshAccessToken.

issues.descricao: Salesforce checks response.statusText !== 'OK' instead of response.ok when refreshing the token, which can misclassify successful responses, and then ignores the refreshed token.
issues.textoGolden: The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: Checks response.statusText !== "OK" instead of response.ok and builds jsforce.Connection from stale credentialKey.access_token/instance_url ignoring accessTokenParsed.data. WHY: Refresh never takes effect (old token reused) and valid refreshes can throw on runtimes where statusText is empty. HOW: Check !response.ok and use parsed access_token/instance_url for connection and DB update.

issues.descricao: After refreshing the Salesforce token, jsforce.Connection is created with the stale access_token and instance_url instead of the newly refreshed values.
issues.textoGolden: The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.

comentarios.texto:
WHAT: The new block fetches and persists a fresh access token (`accessTokenParsed.data`) but then creates the `jsforce.Connection` with the stale `credentialKey.access_token` (line 106) instead of the just-refreshed token.
WHY: The refreshed token is written to the DB but never used for the connection; if the old token was expired, jsforce must refresh again (extra round trip) or fail, and the DB/connection state diverge.
HOW: Pass the new access token (`accessTokenParsed.data.access_token`) to the `jsforce.Connection`.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: canManage() grants write authorization when only the VIEW scope is granted for all groups. WHY: GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup() calls the inherited requireManage(), allowing a view-only administrator to create groups or move an existing child to the top level. HOW: Require MANAGE alone in this method, leaving VIEW acceptance in canView().

WHAT: Group permission enumeration filters by the Groups resource type, but the group-resource creation path never sets that type. WHY: AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource() creates a resource named after the group ID and updates its scopes without setting its type, so newly created per-group VIEW_MEMBERS and MANAGE_MEMBERS permissions are absent from this enumeration and user counts cannot include their members. HOW: Assign the Groups type when creating group authorization resources before relying on findByType().

WHAT: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() uses authorization-resource IDs where model group IDs are required. WHY: AdminPermissionsSchema stores the model group ID in the resource name, while hasPermission() looks up by that name and UsersResource passes the returned IDs to membership queries; using getId() therefore evaluates the wrong resource or all-groups fallback and produces membership filters that match no group. HOW: Use groupResource.getName() for both the permission lookup and the granted set.

WHAT: Wiring the V2 group evaluator into user membership filtering exposes an incompatible legacy JPA query contract. WHY: UsersResource passes the evaluator's group IDs to JpaUserProvider.groupsWithPermissionsSubquery(), which additionally requires a resource named group.resource.<groupId>, whereas the new V2 schema names resources with the bare group ID; even with correctly enumerated IDs, user search and counts exclude permitted members in a V2-only realm. HOW: Update the membership-query resource check to support the V2 naming contract, or remove that legacy existence check when filtering already-authorized V2 group IDs.

The replacement for getGroupsWithViewPermission must still return model group IDs for UsersResource's count and search filters. Here groupResource.getId() is the authorization resource's ID, not the group's ID. Moreover, hasPermission interprets that argument as a resource name (findByName at line 141), so it misses the specific group permission and falls back to all-groups. Use groupResource.getName(), which AdminPermissionsSchema populates with the model group ID, for both evaluation and the returned set. Otherwise group-specific member-view grants fail to expose their users, and any returned authorization IDs cannot match user group membership.

The final check only verifies that joinGroup does not throw. If the endpoint accepts the request but never adds Bob to the group, testManageGroupMembership still passes. Read Bob's groups using the privileged client after this call and assert that topGroup is present, so the test verifies the membership operation as well as authorization.

The new documentation points to canManageMembership, but requireManageMembers enforces canManageMembers. These are distinct permissions (manage-membership versus manage-members), so callers following this contract can expect authorization where the method actually rejects it. Link to canManageMembers instead.

The return documentation says Stream, but the declaration returns Set<String> and both implementations construct or return sets. Describe the actual collection type so callers are not directed to use stream operations or stream lifecycle semantics on the return value.

The schema names each group authorization resource with the model group ID (resolveGroup returns group.getId()), but groupResource.getId() is the authorization resource's own ID. hasPermission then looks that value up by name, missing the specific group resource, and the returned set contains IDs that user searches cannot match to memberships. Use the resource name both for evaluation and for the returned group IDs.

canManage() accepts either VIEW or MANAGE, unlike canManage(group), which requires MANAGE. Consequently an administrator granted only all-groups VIEW passes requireManage() and can create groups through the global management gate. Require MANAGE here so read-only access does not authorize mutations.

AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup uses the GroupModel ID as the authorization resource name, not as its resource ID. Here both the permission lookup and the returned set use groupResource.getId(), which is the authorization resource's separate identifier. hasPermission expects a model group ID and looks up resources by name, and the changed UsersResource passes the returned set to user searches/counts as model group IDs. Consequently a delegate granted view-members/manage-members on a particular group cannot reliably find or count its users (and evaluation may incorrectly fall back to all-groups permissions). Use the resource name for both operations.

issues.descricao: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() accepts the VIEW scope as well as MANAGE, so an admin with only view permission on all groups passes manage checks such as group creation.
issues.textoGolden: In GroupPermissionsV2.canManage(), the permission fallback checks for both VIEW and MANAGE scopes (hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)), but canManage() should only grant access for MANAGE scope, not VIEW. This means users with only VIEW permission on groups can pass the canManage() check, granting them write access they should not have. The canView() method correctly checks both VIEW and MANAGE, but canManage() should only check MANAGE.

comentarios.texto: The no-arg canManage() returns true when the caller holds only an all-groups VIEW permission (`hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE)`), whereas the per-group canManage(GroupModel) (line 79) requires MANAGE. WHAT: a caller with only the view scope on all groups is treated as having manage rights. WHY: canManage()/requireManage() gate group creation and other manage operations (e.g. GroupsResource.addGroup -> auth.groups().requireManage()), so a read-only viewer of all groups can create/manage groups — privilege escalation. HOW: drop VIEW from the scope list so canManage() only returns true for MANAGE, aligning it with canManage(GroupModel): `return hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE);`

GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() (line 70) evaluates hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE), identical to canView() at line 52, so a caller granted only the VIEW scope on the all-groups resource is treated as a group manager. The per-group overload canManage(GroupModel) (line 79) correctly requires only MANAGE, and AdminPermissionsSchema defines MANAGE as the manage scope for GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, so the two checks disagree. requireManage() therefore succeeds for read-only administrators, letting them create/update/delete groups, add subgroups and map group roles. Drop VIEW from the scope list so canManage() checks MANAGE only.

WHAT: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() grants global manage on VIEW scope (hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE)). WHY: A caller with only view-all-groups permission passes the manage check, allowing group creation/management reserved for manage. HOW: Check only MANAGE, e.g. hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE).

issues.descricao: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission uses the authorization resource id instead of the resource name (the group id) for both the permission check and the returned set, so per-group view-members grants are not resolved and user filtering gets wrong ids.
issues.textoGolden: In getGroupIdsWithViewPermission, hasPermission is called with groupResource.getId() and the same groupResource.getId() is added to granted, but hasPermission resolves resources by name (treating the argument as a group id) and the GroupPermissionEvaluator contract says this method returns group IDs that are later used as UserModel.GROUPS and in getUsersCount group filters. This mismatch means per-group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS permissions may not yield the expected group IDs for filtering and counts, and evaluation may effectively only look at the type-level 'all-groups' resource; consider revisiting whether this should operate on the underlying group ids (resource names) instead so it aligns with the JPA queries and the interface contract.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() uses authz resource IDs (groupResource.getId()) as group IDs and looks them up via findByName. WHY: Resource names equal group IDs (AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup returns group.getId()), so findByName(resourceId) misses and the returned set contains unusable IDs, breaking user search/count filtering by group. HOW: Use groupResource.getName() like V1 does (resource.getName().substring prefix / name) for both the hasPermission lookup and the granted set.

findByType callback passes groupResource.getId() to hasPermission() and granted set, but AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup defines resource name (not UUID) as groupId and hasPermission looks up via findByName(server, groupId). Use groupResource.getName() for both check and granted set, otherwise lookups miss to all-groups fallback and callers receive authz UUIDs instead of group IDs.

getGroupIdsWithViewPermission uses groupResource.getId() for lookup and result collection, but V2 group resources are named with the group ID (resolveGroup returns group.getId()) and hasPermission does findByName. Use groupResource.getName() in both places to evaluate the correct per-group resource and to return actual group IDs.

issues.descricao: Per-group resources are created without the Groups type, so getGroupIdsWithViewPermission's findByType never sees specific group grants.

comentarios.texto: findByType(GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE) does not enumerate the specific group resources created by AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource, because that method creates them without setting their type. Consequently, specific VIEW_MEMBERS or MANAGE_MEMBERS grants are omitted from the group IDs used for user counts and database filtering. Assign the Groups type to specific group resources and ensure the all-Groups resource is not treated as a model group.

issues.descricao: The user search filter still requires legacy 'group.resource.<id>' resources, so with V2 group permissions the members of authorized groups are excluded from user searches.

comentarios.texto: The new V2 group permission IDs are passed into a JPA filter that still requires a legacy group.resource.<groupId> authorization resource. JpaUserProvider.groupsWithPermissionsSubquery checks for that prefixed name, whereas AdminPermissionsSchema creates V2 group resources named only with the group ID, so authorized group members are excluded from user searches even with valid group IDs. Update the database filtering path to support V2 resource naming rather than requiring a legacy V1 resource.

issues.descricao: The new Javadoc for requireManageMembers points to canManageMembership instead of canManageMembers.

comentarios.texto: The javadoc for requireManageMembers says it throws ForbiddenException if canManageMembership(GroupModel) returns false, but this method is the require-variant of canManageMembers, not canManageMembership. The Javadoc for requireManageMembers says it throws if canManageMembership(GroupModel) returns false. It should refer to canManageMembers(GroupModel), which is a different check, so the doc misdescribes the method.

Javadoc for requireManageMembers references canManageMembership instead of canManageMembers (copy-paste). Fix link to {@link #canManageMembers(GroupModel)} so the contract describes the method it guards.

@return says 'Stream of IDs' but method returns Set<String> getGroupIdsWithViewPermission. Fix doc to 'Set of IDs' to match the signature.

The new @return documentation promises a Stream of IDs, but the method declares Set<String> and both implementations return sets. Describe a set of IDs instead, so the documented return contract matches what callers actually receive.

sugestoes.texto: The new list item passes only promRule, but RuleActionsButtons.V2 still renders SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer only when rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) is true. Clicking the newly enabled Silence notifications menu item sets showSilenceDrawer without rendering any drawer, so silencing from either list view no longer works. Adapt the drawer path to accept the Prometheus rule UID or load the ruler rule on demand.

canDelete now accepts Prometheus-rule permissions, but the delete menu item still requires rulerRule at line 165. Both new Grafana list paths omit rulerRule, so authorized users lose the Delete action despite canDelete being true. Render deletion using the identifier-based handler for Prometheus-only rules instead of requiring a ruler DTO.

canPause now accepts Prometheus-rule permissions, but rendering MenuItemPauseRule still requires a Grafana rulerRule at line 123. The new Grafana list items never supply that prop, so pause and resume disappear from the list even for editable alert rules. Provide a Prometheus-compatible pause action or fetch the required ruler DTO on demand.

useAllAlertRuleAbilities now delegates to a hook that hardcodes isFederated to false, discarding the previous isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group) check. Legacy RuleActionsButtons uses this wrapper for Update, so federated Mimir rules with source_tenants now receive an Edit action even though they were explicitly immutable before this change. Preserve the combined rule's federation status when computing its abilities.

useAllAlertRuleAbilities previously checked isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group), so callers could rely on Update and Delete being unsupported for federated Mimir groups. This delegation passes only the ruler rule and identifier to an implementation that hardcodes isFederated = false. Consequently existing combined-rule consumers now advertise editing and deleting federated rules whenever datasource permissions allow it. Preserve the federation check in this wrapper or pass the group federation state into the delegated ability calculation.

Finding the rule row waits for the Prometheus response, not the folder-permission response. GrafanaRuleListItem renders its row immediately, whereas useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable initially has no folder and returns isEditable=false. Thus this negative assertion can pass during loading even if the resolved folder permissions are ignored and editing is subsequently allowed. Wait for the folder permission lookup to complete (for example using an observable request-completion signal and flushing its React update) before asserting that Edit is absent, so a regression that grants editing after loading fails this test.

skipToken is converted to undefined, but the underlying hook treats an absent rule as supported once loading is false and grants Duplicate from Grafana create permission. AlertRuleMenu ORs this result with the ruler result, so a datasource rule with duplication unsupported or denied can acquire a Duplicate action simply because the user can create Grafana rules. Return neutral abilities for skipToken after calling the hook.

The previous implementation checked isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group) before allowing Update and Delete. Delegating directly to useAllRulerRuleAbilities now loses that group information; the delegated hook explicitly sets isFederated=false. Existing CombinedRule consumers therefore receive editable/removable abilities for federated groups when ordinary datasource permissions allow them. Preserve the group-level immutability check in this wrapper or pass it to the delegated hook.

AlertRuleMenu passes skipToken for datasource rules and ORs these results with the ruler permissions. However, converting skipToken to undefined does not disable abilities: the new calculator treats an absent rule as non-loading and non-plugin-provided, so Duplicate is supported and allowed whenever the user has Grafana rule-create permission. A datasource rule whose own Duplicate permission is denied can therefore still show that action. Return neutral [false, false] abilities for skipped inputs (in both singular and plural wrappers), while still calling hooks unconditionally.

issues.descricao: The pause menu item is still gated on a Grafana ruler rule, but the list view now passes only the Prometheus rule, so Pause/Resume disappears for list-view rules even when the user may pause them.

comentarios.texto: The new Prometheus-based pause ability cannot display Pause or Resume for list-view rules because the menu still requires rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule) before rendering MenuItemPauseRule. GrafanaRuleListItem now supplies only promRule, so these actions disappear even for editable rules. Adapt the pause menu item to accept the Grafana identifier and Prometheus pause state, or load the ruler rule on demand.

issues.descricao: The Delete menu item still requires a ruler rule, which list-view Grafana rules no longer provide, so users with delete permission lose the Delete action.

comentarios.texto: The new Prometheus-based delete ability is still gated by `canDelete && rulerRule` when rendering the Delete item. Both Grafana list-view paths now omit rulerRule, so users with delete permission lose the Delete action entirely. Render deletion using the available identifier and group identifier instead of requiring the ruler DTO, adapting the callback contract accordingly.

issues.descricao: When the Grafana prom-rule branch is skipped (datasource rules), useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(undefined) still reports Duplicate as supported and allowed by Grafana create permission, and AlertRuleMenu ORs it with the ruler ability, so Duplicate appears on cloud rules even when the ruler check denies it.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: canDuplicate ORs ruler ability with grafana ability where grafana path is skipToken=>undefined for cloud rules, and useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(undefined) returns Duplicate=[true,true] whenever the user has global Grafana create permission. WHY: Any user with Grafana rule-create gets Duplicate menu item on cloud/Mimir rules even when ruler abilities deny it — incorrect authorization gating. HOW: Return NotSupported for all abilities when rule is skipToken/undefined, or gate grafana branch on prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule(promRule) before ORing.

useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities returns AlwaysSupported for Duplicate when rule is undefined (skipToken): loading is false from the !rule early-return, so MaybeSupported=true and duplicateSupported=true. ORed in AlertRuleMenu/RuleActionsButtons this leaks Grafana create permission into non-Grafana rules. Gate MaybeSupported/duplicateSupported on rule existence (e.g. NotSupported when !rule).

useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities must return NotSupported for all actions when rule is undefined (skipToken). Currently MaybeSupported falls back to AlwaysSupported when !loading, so Duplicate=[true, global-create] is true for a cloud rule passed as skipToken, and AlertRuleMenu/RuleActionsButtons OR-logic then incorrectly enables Duplicate (and Explore). Guard with if (!rule) return all-NotSupported abilities or make MaybeSupported require rule.

issues.descricao: The refactor of useAllAlertRuleAbilities into useAllRulerRuleAbilities drops the isFederatedRuleGroup check (isFederated is hardcoded false), so federated Mimir rules are reported as editable and deletable.

comentarios.texto: useAllAlertRuleAbilities now delegates to useAllRulerRuleAbilities, which hardcodes isFederated = false. The previous isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group) check is gone, so federated Mimir rules are no longer treated as immutable and can show edit and delete abilities. Keep the federation check in this wrapper, or pass the federation state into the shared hook.

Delegating useAllAlertRuleAbilities to useAllRulerRuleAbilities discards the group's federation status and replaces the previous isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group) check with a constant false. Legacy RuleActionsButtons consequently enables editing rules in groups with source_tenants, although these groups were explicitly immutable before this change. Preserve the CombinedRule federation check in the wrapper or pass federation status into the delegated ability calculation.

Preserve the federated-group immutability check when delegating this CombinedRule hook. Previously useAllAlertRuleAbilities inspected rule.group with isFederatedRuleGroup and disabled modification/removal for federated rules. The replacement delegates to a hook that hardcodes isFederated=false and receives no group information. Existing useAlertRuleAbility/useAlertRuleAbilities consumers therefore now receive supported update/delete abilities for federated rules when datasource permissions allow them, exposing operations that the previous contract explicitly prohibited. Pass the federation state through or retain that restriction in this wrapper.

issues.descricao: The Grafana prom-rule abilities gate Pause, Restore, Export and DeletePermanently on alertingRule(rule) while the comment claims it checks Grafana-managed rules, so Grafana recording rules lose these actions in the list view.

comentarios.texto: The comment says all GrafanaPromRuleDTO rules are Grafana-managed, but the variable it describes is `isAlertingRule`. That variable is true only for alerting rules and false for Grafana recording rules. Fix the comment, or rename the variable, so it says the check is for alerting rules. As written, readers will expect Pause, Export and Silence to be enabled for recording rules.

The comment says all GrafanaPromRuleDTO rules are Grafana-managed, but the check used is alertingRule(rule), which is false for recording rules. Pause, Restore, ModifyExport and DeletePermanently are therefore wrongly disabled for Grafana recording rules, where the old isGrafanaManagedAlertRule check allowed them. Use prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule(rule) for these abilities, and keep alertingRule only for Silence.

issues.descricao: The comment claims GrafanaPromRuleDTO abilities have no loading state, but the next line makes support depend on the folder loading flag.

comentarios.texto: The comment says there is no loading state, but the next line is `loading ? NotSupported : AlwaysSupported`. `loading` comes from the folder fetch. Update the comment to say that support depends on the folder loading state.

issues.descricao: The Grafana branch of the filtered rule list renders GrafanaRuleListItem without a key prop, so React reconciles the streaming list by index and warns about missing keys.
issues.textoGolden: The rendered GrafanaRuleListItem is missing the required key prop for React list items. This can cause rendering issues when the list order changes.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: The grafana branch of the filtered list renders <GrafanaRuleListItem .../> without a `key` prop, dropping the `key={key}` that the replaced <GrafanaRuleLoader key={key} .../> had. WHY: `rules.map` renders a dynamic list keyed by getRuleKey/hashRule; without a key React logs duplicate-key warnings and reconciles rows by index, so as the async rule stream updates/reorders the wrong rule row can be reused/mutated (stale state, swapped actions). HOW: add `key={key}` (the value is already destructured on line 152) to the <GrafanaRuleListItem> element.

WHAT: Grafana branch of FilterViewResults renders GrafanaRuleListItem without key={key} while datasource and unknown branches pass key. WHY: Breaks React list reconciliation — wrong item reuse, stale actions/state and console key warnings for every Grafana hit. HOW: Add key={key} to the GrafanaRuleListItem element.

issues.descricao: The test named 'should render More button with action menu options' only checks the More button exists, never the menu options.

It finds the button by name 'More', so the aria-label and text assertions are tautological. It would pass even if the menu had no actions or the abilities were broken. Click the button and assert the expected menu items, or rename the test to match what it checks.

Test named 'should render More button with action menu options' never verifies any action menu option: the body only asserts the More button exists and has aria-label/text 'More'. It would still pass if the dropdown were rendered empty (Silence/Duplicate/Copy link/Export all missing), i.e. the behaviour the name promises is not covered. Either open the menu and assert the menu items, or rename the test to reflect that it only checks the trigger button's rendering/accessibility.

Test named 'should render More button with action menu options' never opens the menu nor asserts menu items — it only checks More button presence/aria/text. Click More and assert expected menuitems (or rename to 'should render More button') so it fails if menu actions break.

issues.descricao: GrafanaGroupLoader's JSDoc still says it loads from Prometheus and Ruler endpoints after the ruler query was removed.

comentarios.texto: The JSDoc for GrafanaGroupLoader still says "Loads an evaluation group from Prometheus and Ruler endpoints." but this PR removed the ruler API query entirely — the component now only calls useGetGrafanaGroupsQuery (Prometheus). The documentation describes a data source the function no longer consumes; update it to state only the Prometheus endpoint is loaded (and the same stale "Ruler response" reference in the expectedRulesCount prop doc at lines 18–19 should be corrected).

issues.descricao: For list-view Grafana rules RuleActionsButtons gets only promRule, so the Silence menu item is shown but the silence drawer, still gated on a ruler alerting rule, never renders and clicking Silence does nothing.
issues.textoGolden: RuleActionsButtons is invoked with only promRule, but SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer inside RuleActionsButtons still depends on a Grafana Ruler rule being present, so for Grafana rules coming from list views the 'Silence notifications' menu entry (now driven by Grafana Prom abilities) will toggle showSilenceDrawer without ever rendering the drawer. This means clicking 'Silence notifications' for these rules has no visible effect, even when abilities indicate silencing is allowed.

comentarios.texto: Passing only promRule enables the Silence notifications menu item but leaves RuleActionsButtons.V2 unable to render its silence drawer, which is guarded by rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule). Clicking Silence only updates showSilenceDrawer and displays nothing because rule is undefined. Update the drawer to accept a rule UID—the inspected SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer only needs grafana_alert.uid—and allow the Prometheus alerting-rule path to render it.

The new list item passes only promRule to RuleActionsButtons, but that component renders SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer only under `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) && showSilenceDrawer`. With rule undefined, clicking the newly enabled 'Silence notifications' action only sets state and never opens a drawer. Adapt the silence rendering path to load/use the rule by its Prometheus identifier before switching this caller to promRule-only.

WHAT: getEditableIdentifier now enables a prom-only path (Grafana uid identifier with rulerRule undefined) but the silence drawer still renders only when rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) is true. WHY: In the list view Silence menu item can be shown via grafana abilities, clicking it sets showSilenceDrawer but the drawer never mounts, so Silence silently does nothing. HOW: Gate the drawer on promRule as well or provide a prom-based silence drawer.

sugestoes.texto: MetricAlertDetectorHandler now inherits abstract stateful methods without implementing them. MetricAlertFire still registers this class, so Detector.detector_handler calls its constructor and raises TypeError for metric_alert_fire detectors, aborting process_detectors before evaluation. Keep this handler concrete with a dictionary-returning no-op evaluate implementation until its stateful methods and occurrence builder are implemented.

The expected occurrence is built for "val1", but test_dedupe evaluates "group_key". The new hook builds the actual occurrence using the evaluated key, so its fingerprint differs from the expected occurrence and the equality assertion fails. Build the expected occurrence with "group_key".

Switching this empty handler to StatefulDetectorHandler leaves its abstract counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, and build_occurrence_and_event_data unimplemented. Instantiating MetricAlertDetectorHandler now raises TypeError, so obtaining a handler for the registered metric-alert group type breaks before evaluation. Retain the concrete no-op handler until the stateful hooks are implemented, or implement all required hooks here.

Changing this handler to StatefulDetectorHandler while leaving its body empty makes it abstract. That base requires get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, and the newly added build_occurrence_and_event_data hook. Instantiating the registered metric-alert detector handler now raises TypeError instead of providing the previous no-op evaluation. Keep the handler concrete with the dictionary-returning no-op evaluate contract until its stateful hooks are implemented, or implement all required hooks here.

MetricAlertDetectorHandler was previously concrete, but switching it to StatefulDetectorHandler without implementing its abstract members makes it non-instantiable. In particular, this PR adds the required abstract build_occurrence_and_event_data method, while this subclass contains only pass. Accessing Detector.detector_handler for the registered metric-alert group type now raises TypeError rather than returning the previous no-op handler, so process_detectors fails before evaluation. Keep the no-op handler concrete (with the updated dictionary return contract) until the stateful hooks are implemented.

The docstring immediately below still says this method returns a list of DetectorEvaluationResult, but this change returns a dictionary keyed by DetectorGroupKey. Callers following that documentation would iterate keys rather than results. Update the return-shape description to match the new contract.

The adjacent TODO says this will become a stateful detector when the abstraction is built, but the class now inherits that very abstraction. Remove or revise the TODO so it describes the remaining implementation work rather than a future conversion already completed.
